checked_claims.claim: Async stack serializes concurrent requests and uses exponential backoff
checked_claims.reason: Construction order is not global request serialization; cache lock is per constructed middleware after network await; backoff is fixed asyncio.sleep.

material_errors: Construction order is not global request serialization; cache lock is per constructed middleware after network await; backoff is fixed asyncio.sleep.
tasks.notes: Independent static inspection of pinned source; repository code was not executed. Scope is central claims, not exhaustive runtime verification.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The premise is not established. async_combine_middlewares constructs a nested callable chain (web3/middleware/__init__.py:110-124); ordered processing within a request does not serialize separate coroutines. Optional async cache middleware awaits the network request before locking only the cache update (web3/middleware/async_cache.py:60-88). Async retry awaits make_request and sleeps a fixed backoff_factor between eligible retries, allowing the event loop to run other tasks (web3/middleware/exception_retry_request.py:147-160). Middleware work, lock contention and retries can add costs, but throughput bottlenecks require profiling. AutoProvider discovery is a separate provider path, not an inherent AsyncHTTPProvider stage.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: At this revision hexbytes>=0.1.0, lru-dict>=1.1.6 and websockets>=10.0.0 have lower bounds without upper bounds (setup.py:70-86). Development dependencies mix policies: flake8 and types-protobuf are exact pins, while black, isort, mypy and many others have lower bounds; towncrier has a range (12-42). Exact pins constrain selected versions while lower bounds permit newer releases, but these declarations do not document why each bound was selected or ensure reproducibility of the whole environment. The release note records removal of GPL pylru and qualified MIT compliance (docs/releases.rst:3000), not a general pinning policy.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: HTTPProvider stores request_kwargs and forwards them on each make_request. get_request_kwargs adds default headers only when callers supplied no headers; it does not merge custom headers with defaults (web3/providers/rpc.py:62,72-92). AsyncHTTPProvider follows the same pattern (web3/providers/async_rpc.py:63,73-93). Retry middleware repeats the wrapped request for eligible methods/errors, so configured request arguments are reused (web3/middleware/exception_retry_request.py:147-160). This is generic HTTP plumbing; these paths do not implement AWS credential discovery, signing, token renewal, or a guarantee that expired credentials remain valid.
